correctness.rationale: A vertex subset of the rook graph is exactly an edge subset of K_{m,n}; its induced graph is a forest exactly when the selected bipartite edge subgraph is a disjoint union of paths. The component EGF counts singleton, odd-edge alternating, and even-edge alternating paths without overcounting reversal. Applying the labeled exponential formula gives the exact formal series. Degree at most twice the smaller shore, with a balanced forest cap, is attained by explicit alternating paths. Balanced extremals are precisely alternating Hamiltonian paths; unbalanced extremals biject to labeled path forests on the larger shore with one smaller-shore label per edge, yielding the stated finite binomial sum. Independent native-graph exhaustive checks and exact-rational coefficient expansions corroborated all checked cases. Remaining limit: finite checks do not replace the infinite bijective proof.

value.rationale: Acyclic induced-subgraph polynomials are natural refinements of feedback-vertex-set optimization. This result determines every coefficient simultaneously for all rectangular rook graphs and counts every minimum feedback vertex set by a new factorial/binomial expression, with a meaningful balanced-versus-unbalanced extremal classification. Unlike a tabulated minimum or an arbitrary finite computation, it supplies an exact two-parameter generating law and structural bijection that can support enumeration and random sampling.
